class.name: Dimensionalist (Book of Classes)
class.proficiency: Intelligence, Wisdom, History, Investigation, Insight, Perception, Nature

trait.name: Dimensionalist
trait.text:
Dimensionalists study the hidden distances between places, moments, and worlds. To them, an empty doorway may preserve the memory of another destination, a shadow may lean toward a distant plane, and a single heartbeat may contain several possible outcomes. Some learn through observatories, sealed archives, or ancient planar engines. Others follow wandering thresholds that appear only during eclipses, storms, or dreams. Through calculation and dangerous experimentation, a Dimensionalist learns to loosen reality without allowing it to tear completely apart.
Source: Book of Classes (Homebrew)

feature.name: Starting Dimensionalist
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Dimensionalist, you begin play with 6 + your Constitution modifier hit points.
You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.
• Armor: none • Weapons: Simple weapons • Tools: none • Skills: Choose 2 from History, Investigation, Insight, Perception, and Nature
You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment provided by your background.
• (a) a quarterstaff or (b) a dagger • (a) a component pouch or (b) an arcane focus, which can take the form of an ethereal crystal shard • (a) a scholar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack • A Dimensional Tome
If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 4d4 × 10 gp to buy your equipment.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Multiclass Wizard
feature.text:
If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose dimensionalist as one of your classes.
Ability Score Minimum: As a multiclass character, you must have at least the following ability score(s) to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a dimensionalist.
• Intelligence 13
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Multiclass Features
feature.text:
When you gain a new level in a class, you get its features for that level. You don't, however, receive the class's starting equipment, and a few features have additional rules when you're multiclassing: Channel Divinity, Extra Attack, Unarmored Defense, and Spellcasting.
Channel Divinity: If you already have the Channel Divinity feature and gain a level in a class that also grants the feature, you gain the Channel Divinity effects granted by that class, but getting the feature again doesn't give you an additional use of it. You gain additional uses only when you reach a class level that explicitly grants them to you. For example, if you are a cleric 6/paladin 4, you can use Channel Divinity twice between rests because you are high enough level in the cleric class to have more uses. Whenever you use the feature, you can choose any of the Channel Divinity effects available to you from your two classes.
Extra Attack: If you gain the Extra Attack class feature from more than one class, the features don't add together. You can't make more than two attacks with this feature unless it says you do (as the fighter's version of Extra Attack does). Similarly, the warlock's eldritch invocation Thirsting Blade doesn't give you additional attacks if you also have Extra Attack.
Unarmored Defense: If you already have the Unarmored Defense feature, you can't gain it again from another class.
Spellcasting: Your capacity for spellcasting depends partly on your combined levels in all your spellcasting classes and partly on your individual levels in those classes. Once you have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class, use the rules below. If you multiclass but have the Spellcasting feature from only one class, you follow the rules as described in that class.
Spells Known and Prepared: You determine what spells you know and can prepare for each class individually, as if you were a single-classed member of that class. If you are a ranger 4/wizard 3, for example, you know three 1 st-level ranger spells based on your levels in the ranger class. As a 3rd-level wizard, you know three wizard cantrips, and your spellbook contains ten wizard spells, two of which (the two you gained when you reached 3rd level as a wizard) can be 2nd-level spells. If your Intelligence is 16, you can prepare six wizard spells from your spellbook. Each spell you know and prepare is associated with one of your classes, and you use the spell casting ability of that class when you cast the spell. Similarly, a spellcasting focus, such as a holy symbol, can be used only for the spells from the class associated with that focus. If a cantrip of yours increases in power at higher levels, the increase is based on your character level, not your level in a particular class.
Spell Slots: You determine your available spell slots by adding together all your levels in the bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, and wizard classes, half your levels (rounded down) in the paladin and ranger classes, and a third of your fighter or rogue levels (rounded down) if you have the Eldritch Knight or the Arcane Trickster feature. Use this total to determine your spell slots by consulting the Multiclass Spellcaster table. If you have more than one spellcasting class, this table might give you spell slots of a level that is higher than the spells you know or can prepare. You can use those slots, but only to cast your lower-level spells. If a lower level spell that you cast, like burning hands, has an enhanced effect when cast using a higher-level slot, you can use the enhanced effect, even though you don't have any spells of that higher level. For example, if you are the aforementioned ranger 4/ wizard 3, you count as a 5th-level character when determining your spell slots: you have four 1st-level slots, three 2nd-level slots, and two 3rd-level slots. However, you don't know any 3rd-level spells, nor do you know any 2nd-level ranger spells. You can use the spell slots of those levels to cast the spells you do know-and potentially enhance their effects.
Pact Magic: If you have both the Spellcasting class feature and the Pact Magic class feature from the warlock class, you can use the spell slots you gain from the Pact Magic feature to cast spells you know or have prepared from classes with the Spellcasting class feature, and you can use the spell slots you gain from the Spellcasting class feature to cast warlock spells you know.
Source: Player's Handbook (2014) p. 164

feature.name: Dimensioncasting
feature.text:
You pry at the seams of space. You are a Dimensionalist spellcaster. You prepare spells from those recorded in your Dimensional Tome and cast them using the spell slots shown in the Dimensionalist table.
Cantrips: You know three cantrips of your choice from the Dimensionalist spell list. You learn additional Dimensionalist cantrips as shown in the Dimensionalist table.
Dimensional Tome: At 1st level, your Dimensional Tome contains six 1st-level Dimensionalist spells of your choice. Whenever you gain a level in this class after 1st, you add one Dimensionalist spell of your choice to the tome. The spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots. You cannot add spells to your Dimensional Tome except through this class's features. If your tome is lost or destroyed, you can replace it when you finish a long rest. The replacement contains every spell that was recorded in the previous tome, which becomes blank if it still exists.
Replacing Spells: Whenever you gain a level in this class after 1st, you can choose one Dimensionalist spell recorded in your Dimensional Tome and replace it with another spell from the Dimensionalist spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
Prepared Spells: You prepare a number of Dimensionalist spells equal to your Intelligence modifier + your Dimensionalist level, with a minimum of one spell. Each prepared spell must be recorded in your Dimensional Tome and must be of a level for which you have spell slots. You can change your prepared spells when you finish a long rest.
Spell Slots: The Dimensionalist table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Dimensionalist spells of 1st level or higher. To cast one of those spells, you must expend a spell slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
Ritual Casting: You can cast a Dimensionalist spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and is recorded in your Dimensional Tome. You do not need to have the spell prepared.
Spellcasting Ability: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Dimensionalist spells, since your magic is shaped through calculation, focus, and higher-dimensional theory. You use your Intelligence whenever a Dimensionalist spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a Dimensionalist spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.
Spellcasting Focus: You can use an arcane focus or your Dimensional Tome as a spellcasting focus for your Dimensionalist spells.
Source: Book of Classes p. 226 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Dimensional Scholar
feature.text:
You've glimpsed the latticework of the planes. You gain proficiency in Arcana. If you already have proficiency in Arcana, choose one other skill from the class list and gain proficiency in it instead. Furthermore, when you make an Intelligence (Arcana) check about portals, planes, teleportation circles, or extraplanar creatures, you treat a d20 roll of 7 or lower as an 8.
Source: Book of Classes p. 226 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Rift Reserve
feature.text:
Each spell leaves a pressure behind where reality was forced to bend. You have a number of rift charges equal to your proficiency bonus + half your Intelligence modifier, rounded up after halving that modifier. If this total would be lower than your proficiency bonus, your number of rift charges equals your proficiency bonus instead. You regain all expended rift charges when you finish a long rest. When initiative is rolled and you have no rift charges remaining, you regain one rift charge. You cannot have more rift charges than your maximum.
Source: Book of Classes p. 226 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Dimensional Warp
feature.text:
Reality creases around a nearby outline, carrying a creature through a distance too small for the world to notice. As a bonus action, you can expend one rift charge and choose yourself or one willing creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target teleports up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. The teleportation distance increases to 15 feet at 5th level, 20 feet at 11th level, and 30 feet at 17th level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 226 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Studies
feature.text:
Your research commits to one strain of higher-dimensional theory, shaping the way your magic behaves. Choose one Study: Study of Reality, Study of Time, or Study of the Planes. Your choice grants features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level. Each subclass also has an expanded spell list. The spells of your chosen subclass are added to the class's spell list for you.
Source: Book of Classes p. 226 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1, or you can choose a feat. You cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows it, you can choose your class's optional feature at 4th level instead of increasing an ability score or choosing a feat. If you do, you gain that optional feature's 4th-level benefit. You cannot choose this optional feature for the first time at 8th level or higher. At 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you choose either the corresponding benefit of that optional feature or an Ability Score Improvement or feat. If you choose an Ability Score Improvement or feat at one of those levels, you forfeit the optional feature's benefit at that level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Astral Compass (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
A palm-sized compass of dull brass ticks without gears, its needle trembling toward things no map admits. In caves, it leans toward gaps behind stone; in cities, it favors alleys that should not connect; in the wild, it drifts toward the path that spares your blood. It does not point to a place-it points to a way.
Source: Book of Classes p. 235 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Unmapped Needle (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
The compass settles into your palm as though it has always known you. Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain the Astral Compass, a magical object. While holding it, you always know which way is north, have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to navigate, and have advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks made to locate secret doors, hidden passages, or concealed openings. If the compass is lost or destroyed, you can replace it when you finish a long rest. When you do so, any previous compass created by this feature becomes a nonmagical object. While holding the compass, you can use each of the following readings once, and you regain both uses when you finish a long rest:
Open Way: As an action, you learn the direction of the nearest doorway, passage, or staircase within 60 feet through which you could pass without squeezing.
Hidden Draft: As an action, you learn the direction of the nearest secret door, hidden passage, or concealed opening within 30 feet, if one exists. You do not learn its distance, nature, or precise location.
Source: Book of Classes p. 235 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Interdimensional Portal
feature.text:
Two windows unfold in the air, each revealing the world from the other's position. As an action, choose two different points you can see within 60 feet, each on a solid surface large enough to hold a circular opening 10 feet in diameter. A pair of linked portals appears at those points until the start of your next turn. Each portal is large enough to admit a Large or smaller creature. A willing Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of either portal can spend 5 feet of movement to enter it. The creature teleports to an unoccupied space of its choice within 5 feet of the other portal that it can occupy. If no such space is available, the creature cannot enter the portal. A creature can teleport through the portals only once during this use of the feature. You can use this feature once, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. At 11th level, the range increases to 120 feet, and you can use this feature twice between long rests.
Source: Book of Classes p. 226 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Fold Through Restraints
feature.text:
Chains and grasping limbs lose their certainty when nearby bodies slip between positions. You have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to avoid or end the grappled or restrained condition when that condition is caused by a creature's physical grasp or a nonmagical object. In addition, immediately before you teleport yourself using a Dimensionalist feature or a spell of 1st level or higher, you can end the grappled condition on yourself, and you can end the restrained condition on yourself if it was caused by a creature's physical grasp or a nonmagical object. When you teleport a willing creature using Dimensional Warp, you can also end the grappled condition on that creature, and you can end the restrained condition on it if the condition was caused by a creature's physical grasp or a nonmagical object. When either condition ends in this way, the creature or object causing it remains behind and does not teleport with the target.
Source: Book of Classes p. 227 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1, or you can choose a feat. You cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows it, you can choose your class's optional feature at 4th level instead of increasing an ability score or choosing a feat. If you do, you gain that optional feature's 4th-level benefit. You cannot choose this optional feature for the first time at 8th level or higher. At 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you choose either the corresponding benefit of that optional feature or an Ability Score Improvement or feat. If you choose an Ability Score Improvement or feat at one of those levels, you forfeit the optional feature's benefit at that level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Tuned Bearing (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
The compass clicks softly, as though remembering the shape of what you name. Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. As an action while holding the compass, choose one creature or specific object you have seen within the past 30 days. For 1 hour, the needle points toward the target while it is within 5 miles of you and on the same plane of existence. The compass does not reveal the target's distance or a safe route to it, and it cannot detect a target protected from divination magic. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Dimensional Shatter
feature.text:
Your spell opens a second wound beside the first, wrenching one victim through a violent fold. Once on each of your turns, when one or more creatures take damage from a Dimensionalist spell of 1st level or higher that you cast, you can choose one of those creatures and expend one rift charge. The chosen creature takes additional force damage equal to 1d8 + your proficiency bonus and must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you teleport it up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that it can occupy without falling.
Source: Book of Classes p. 227 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Unstable Reality
feature.text:
Your spells no longer need to begin where you stand, for you can open a momentary aperture and cast through it. When you cast a Dimensionalist spell with a range other than Self, or a Dimensionalist spell with a range of Self that creates a cone, cube, or line as part of its casting, you can expend one rift charge to create an aperture in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you. For that casting, treat the aperture as your space when determining the spell's range, cover, clear path to a target, and point of origin. If the spell has a range of Touch, you can target a creature or object within 5 feet of the aperture as if you were within 5 feet of it. If the spell has a range of Self, the cone, cube, or line created as part of the casting originates from the aperture instead of you. You remain the spell's caster, must still provide its components, and must still see any target or point that the spell requires you to see. The aperture is not a creature or object, and you do not occupy its space. The aperture vanishes immediately after the spell is cast.
Source: Book of Classes p. 227 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1, or you can choose a feat. You cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows it, you can choose your class's optional feature at 4th level instead of increasing an ability score or choosing a feat. If you do, you gain that optional feature's 4th-level benefit. You cannot choose this optional feature for the first time at 8th level or higher. At 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you choose either the corresponding benefit of that optional feature or an Ability Score Improvement or feat. If you choose an Ability Score Improvement or feat at one of those levels, you forfeit the optional feature's benefit at that level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Marked Waypoint (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
You press the compass against the ground, and its needle fixes your position within the hidden geometry of the world. Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. As an action while holding the compass, mark your current location as a waypoint for 7 days. While you are on the same plane of existence, you always know the direction and approximate distance of the waypoint. You can have only one waypoint at a time, and creating another causes the previous waypoint to disappear. Once before the waypoint disappears, while you are within 1 mile of it and holding the compass, you can use an action to teleport yourself and one willing creature within 5 feet of you. Each target appears in a different unoccupied space it can occupy at the waypoint or in the nearest available unoccupied space it can occupy. After you teleport in this way, the waypoint disappears. Once you create a waypoint, you cannot create another until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Greater Teleportation
feature.text:
Distance folds broadly enough to carry more than one traveler through the same crease. When you use Dimensional Warp, you can expend one additional rift charge to choose a second willing Large or smaller creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The second target can be yourself, but it cannot be the same creature as the first target. Each target teleports up to the distance allowed by Dimensional Warp to a different unoccupied space you can see. If no such space is available for the second target, you cannot choose it. In addition, the range of Interdimensional Portal increases to 300 feet, provided you can see both points where the portals appear.
Source: Book of Classes p. 227 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Reality Bender
feature.text:
Your position fractures at the instant a blow should land, forcing the attacker to strike another possibility. When an attack roll hits you, but before the attack's damage or other effects are resolved, you can use your reaction and expend two rift charges to teleport up to the distance allowed by Dimensional Warp to an unoccupied space you can see. If you are outside the attack's range or otherwise no longer a valid target from your new position, the triggering attack misses you. Otherwise, the attacker rerolls the attack roll against you from its original space and must use the new result. Resolve the reroll using your new position, including any changes to the attack's range, your cover, and any advantage or disadvantage.
Source: Book of Classes p. 227 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1, or you can choose a feat. You cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows it, you can choose your class's optional feature at 4th level instead of increasing an ability score or choosing a feat. If you do, you gain that optional feature's 4th-level benefit. You cannot choose this optional feature for the first time at 8th level or higher. At 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you choose either the corresponding benefit of that optional feature or an Ability Score Improvement or feat. If you choose an Ability Score Improvement or feat at one of those levels, you forfeit the optional feature's benefit at that level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Impossible Passage (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
The needle turns toward paths hidden inside stone, wood, and earth, revealing openings that exist only from the proper angle. Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. As an action while holding the compass, choose yourself and up to five willing creatures you can see within 30 feet. For 1 minute, each target can move through up to 5 feet of nonmagical solid objects, structures, or terrain once. Moving through such material costs 1 additional foot of movement for each foot traveled. A target cannot end its movement inside such material. If it would do so, it returns to the last unoccupied space it occupied before entering the material. If that space is occupied, it appears in the nearest unoccupied space it can occupy on the same side of the material from which it entered. In either case, it takes 2d10 force damage. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Multiverse Mastery
feature.text:
Countless outcomes flare before you, and you seize the reality in which your spell finds its mark. When you miss with a spell attack made as part of a Dimensionalist spell, you can reroll the attack roll and must use the new roll. Alternatively, when a creature succeeds on a saving throw against a Dimensionalist spell you cast, you can force that creature to reroll the saving throw and use the new roll. You cannot use this feature if the creature succeeded without rolling, or if it failed the saving throw and then chose to succeed instead. You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 227 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1, or you can choose a feat. You cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows it, you can choose your class's optional feature at 4th level instead of increasing an ability score or choosing a feat. If you do, you gain that optional feature's 4th-level benefit. You cannot choose this optional feature for the first time at 8th level or higher. At 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you choose either the corresponding benefit of that optional feature or an Ability Score Improvement or feat. If you choose an Ability Score Improvement or feat at one of those levels, you forfeit the optional feature's benefit at that level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: The Shortest Road (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
The needle becomes perfectly still, and the world briefly stops arguing about the path ahead. Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. As an action while holding the compass, choose yourself and up to five willing creatures you can see within 30 feet. Choose a specific location on your current plane of existence that you have previously visited. Each target teleports to a different unoccupied space it can occupy at that location or in the nearest available unoccupied space it can occupy. This travel cannot arrive off target or cause a teleportation mishap. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 224 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Dimensional Ascendance
feature.text:
Horizons wrinkle at your approach, and every nearby location becomes another place you might already occupy. At the start of each of your turns, provided you are not incapacitated, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see without using an action or expending a rift charge. When initiative is rolled, you regain all expended rift charges. In addition, you cannot be teleported, transported to another plane, or moved by magical means against your will. You can choose to allow any such effect to affect you.
Source: Book of Classes p. 227 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Studies: Study of Reality
feature.text:
Your studies reveal that the world is only one arrangement among many. You fracture stable forms, overlap possible positions, and force reality to reconsider what it had already decided.
Reality Expanded Spell List: Spell Level | Spells 2nd | Magic Weapon, Shatter, Web 3rd | Meld into Stone, Plant Growth, Wind Wall 4th | Fabricate, Polymorph 5th | Creation, Passwall, Wall of Force 6th | Flesh to Stone, Move Earth 7th | Mirage Arcane, Sequester 8th | Feeblemind, Glibness 9th | Weird, Wish
Source: Book of Classes p. 228 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Splinter Step (Study of Reality)
feature.text:
Your body separates into several out-of-phase possibilities whenever danger closes around you. When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can use your reaction before the attack roll is made to impose disadvantage on the roll. After the attack is resolved, if you are not incapacitated, you can teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. If the attack misses, the next time you damage the attacker with a Dimensionalist spell before the end of your next turn, it takes an additional 1d6 force damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 228 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Unreality Lash (Study of Reality)
feature.text:
A jagged seam snaps across the battlefield, distorting movement and thought wherever it passes. As an action, choose up to two creatures you can see within 30 feet. Each target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a target takes 3d8 psychic damage, its speed is halved, and it cannot take reactions until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers no other effect. The damage increases to 4d8 when you reach 14th level in this class. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 228 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Phase Mantle (Study of Reality)
feature.text:
A veil of overlapping possibilities settles over you, leaving observers uncertain which outline belongs to the present. As a bonus action, you cloak yourself for 1 minute. Opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage for the duration. Once on each of your turns while the mantle lasts, when you teleport, when you teleport a creature using Dimensional Warp, or when a Dimensionalist spell of 1st level or higher that you cast causes at least one creature to teleport, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier, with a minimum of 1 temporary hit point. You can then choose one hostile creature you can see within 10 feet of you or within 10 feet of one creature teleported by that trigger. It takes force damage equal to your proficiency bonus. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 228 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Fracture Field (Study of Reality)
feature.text:
You fasten a region of broken space in place, where every step catches against a different version of the ground. As an action, create a 15-foot cube at a point you can see within 60 feet. The field lasts for 1 minute and is difficult terrain for hostile creatures. The first time on a turn that a hostile creature enters the field or starts its turn there, it must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. It takes 2d8 force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. On a failed save, it also cannot take reactions until the start of its next turn. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 228 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Paradox (Study of Reality)
feature.text:
Possible outcomes gather around you like reflections in shattered glass. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction after seeing the roll but before its outcome is determined. The creature rerolls the d20, and you choose which of the two rolls is used. After the triggering attack, ability check, or saving throw and its immediate effects are resolved, if the creature remains within 30 feet of you, you can teleport it up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. If the chosen roll caused the attack to hit or the creature to succeed on the ability check or saving throw, the creature must be willing. If the chosen roll caused the attack to miss or the creature to fail the ability check or saving throw, you can teleport it whether it is willing or unwilling. You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 228 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Studies: Study of the Planes
feature.text:
Through study, exposure, or dangerous correspondence, you have formed a lasting bond with one plane of existence. Its substance clings to your magic and answers when you call.
Planes Expanded Spell List: Spell Level | Spells 2nd | Heat Metal, Moonbeam, Spiritual Weapon 3rd | Call Lightning, Daylight, Stinking Cloud 4th | Conjure Minor Elementals, Guardian of Faith 5th | Conjure Elemental, Hallow, Planar Binding 6th | Planar Ally, Word of Recall 7th | Conjure Celestial, Divine Word 8th | Control Weather, Holy Aura 9th | Storm of Vengeance, Weird
Source: Book of Classes p. 230 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Planar Bond (Study of the Planes)
feature.text:
A fault line from a distant realm runs through your magic, lending its substance to every spell you shape. Choose one plane from the Planar Bond options below. You gain resistance to the damage type associated with that plane, which is your planar damage type. The listed spell is always prepared for you, does not count against the number of spells you can prepare, and does not need to be recorded in your Dimensional Tome. It counts as a Dimensionalist spell for you. You can change your chosen plane whenever you gain a level in this class.
Feywild: Your planar damage type is psychic, and suggestion is your bond spell.
Shadowfell: Your planar damage type is necrotic, and darkness is your bond spell.
Elemental Fire: Your planar damage type is fire, and flaming sphere is your bond spell.
Elemental Water: Your planar damage type is cold, and alter self is your bond spell.
Elemental Earth: Your planar damage type is acid, and acid arrow is your bond spell.
Elemental Air: Your planar damage type is lightning, and gust of wind is your bond spell.
Astral Plane: Your planar damage type is radiant, and detect thoughts is your bond spell.
Source: Book of Classes p. 230 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Planar Reprisal (Study of the Planes)
feature.text:
Your bonded plane surges through a wound, folding the threatened creature away as foreign energy lashes back. When you or a willing ally you can see within 30 feet would take damage, you can use your reaction after the damage is determined but before it is applied. Reduce the damage by an amount equal to 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier, with a minimum reduction of 1. You can then teleport yourself or the creature that would take the damage up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that the teleporting creature can occupy. Any remaining damage is then applied to the creature that would have taken it. If the damage was dealt by a creature you could see within 60 feet when you used this reaction, that creature takes damage of your planar damage type equal to your proficiency bonus. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 230 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Planar Rally (Study of the Planes)
feature.text:
The presence of your bonded realm spreads around you, replacing hostile ground with familiar paths. As a bonus action, choose up to two willing creatures you can see within 30 feet of you, which can include yourself. For 1 minute, you ignore difficult terrain. For the duration, each chosen creature gains resistance to your planar damage type and ignores difficult terrain while it is within 30 feet of you. Also for the duration, once on each of your turns, immediately after you cast a Dimensionalist spell of 1st level or higher, you can teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 230 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Breach Carousel (Study of the Planes)
feature.text:
You open two wounds in the world and stitch their distant edges together. As an action, choose two different points you can see within 60 feet, each on a solid surface large enough to hold a circular opening 10 feet in diameter. A pair of linked rifts appears at those points for 1 minute. Each rift is large enough to admit a Large or smaller creature. When a Large or smaller creature enters either rift, it immediately teleports to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the other rift that it can occupy. A creature that enters willingly chooses this destination. When a creature enters through forced movement, you choose its destination, and the forced movement ends immediately after the creature teleports. If no suitable space is available, the creature does not enter the rift, its movement ends immediately before it, and it does not teleport. A creature can teleport through these rifts only once on each turn. The first time on a turn that a hostile creature enters either rift, it must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. It takes 3d8 damage of your planar damage type on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. On a failed save, it is also pushed 10 feet away from the destination rift. A creature can take this damage only once per round. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 231 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Sovereign Threshold (Study of the Planes)
feature.text:
Your presence becomes a living border between worlds, granting safe passage to allies and exposing enemies to your bonded realm. As an action, you create a 30-foot aura centered on yourself for 1 minute. The aura moves with you. When you or an ally teleports from a space within the aura or into a space within the aura, the teleporting creature gains resistance to your planar damage type until the start of its next turn. Immediately after teleporting, it can also move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. Once on each of your turns, before a hostile creature in the aura makes a saving throw against a Dimensionalist spell you cast, you can impose disadvantage on that saving throw. You can impose disadvantage in this way a number of times during the aura equal to your Intelligence modifier, with a minimum of once. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 231 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Studies: Study of Time
feature.text:
You feel the hinge of each moment and lean upon it, letting the next second arrive early or forcing the last second to linger beyond its proper end.
Time Expanded Spell List: Spell Level | Spells 2nd | Augury, Gentle Repose, Lesser Restoration 3rd | Haste, Revivify, Slow 4th | Death Ward, Divination 5th | Legend Lore, Modify Memory, Raise Dead 6th | Contingency, Programmed Illusion 7th | Regenerate, Sequester 8th | Feeblemind, Mind Blank 9th | Weird, True Resurrection
Source: Book of Classes p. 229 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Rewind the Count (Study of Time)
feature.text:
You hear the first heartbeat of battle before anyone else realizes it has begun. After initiative is rolled but before the first turn begins, provided you are not incapacitated or surprised, you can place yourself at initiative count 20 for the first round. If your rolled initiative is higher than 20, you can retain that initiative instead. If this places you at the same initiative count as another creature, resolve the tie normally. You take only one turn during the first round. At the beginning of the second round, you return to the initiative count you originally rolled. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 229 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Time-Lapse Strike (Study of Time)
feature.text:
You cut a fragment from a creature's next moment, leaving its actions to arrive separately and out of order. As an action, make a ranged spell attack against one creature within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes 4d8 force damage and must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, until the end of its next turn, its speed is halved, it cannot take reactions, and it can take either an action or a bonus action on its turn, but not both. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 229 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Temporal Anchor (Study of Time)
feature.text:
You pin your present location to an invisible point in time, preserving it against the next violent change. As a bonus action, mark your current location for 1 minute. The mark is fixed to the surface or object supporting you, or fixed in space if nothing is supporting you. Once before the anchor ends, when damage is determined for you but before it is applied, or when you fail a saving throw but before suffering the effects of the failure, you can use your reaction, provided you are within 300 feet of the marked location and on the same plane of existence as it. If damage triggered the reaction, reduce that damage by an amount equal to 2d8 + your Intelligence modifier, with a minimum reduction of 1. If a failed saving throw triggered it, reroll the saving throw and you must use the new result. You then return to the marked location. If that location is occupied, you appear in an unoccupied space of your choice within 5 feet of it. If no such space is available, you remain in your current space. After you teleport, the triggering attack, spell, or other effect continues to resolve normally, using the reduced damage or the new saving throw result as appropriate. The anchor then ends. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 229 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Echo Cast (Study of Time)
feature.text:
The final instant of your spell remains caught in time, waiting for you to release it again. When you cast a Dimensionalist spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or lower, and that spell has a casting time of 1 action and an instantaneous duration, you can preserve an echo of the spell. On your next turn, you can use your action to cast the spell again at the same level without expending a spell slot. The echo repeats the same targets, distribution among those targets, point of origin, direction, destination, damage type, and any other choices made for the original casting. Each target and required point must still be legal and within range for the echo's casting. Any original target that is no longer legal or within range is unaffected, and if no target or required point remains legal and within range, you cannot release the echo. If the spell has a range of Self and creates an area, that area must originate from the same space as it did during the original casting. If the original spell was cast through an aperture created by Unstable Reality, the echo can use the aperture's space as its repeated point of origin only if that point of origin would still be legal without the aperture. You make new attack rolls, and affected creatures make new saving throws. You must provide any required material components again. The echo disappears at the end of that turn if you do not release it. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 229 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Hour Sovereign (Study of Time)
feature.text:
You impose a measured rhythm upon the battlefield, hastening chosen lives while forcing others through resistant seconds. As an action, you create a 30-foot aura centered on yourself for 1 minute. The aura moves with you. You and your allies in the aura gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws. At the start of each of your turns, you can choose yourself or one ally you can see in the aura. Until the start of your next turn, the chosen creature's speed increases by 20 feet, and it gains one additional reaction that it can use even if it has already used its normal reaction. The creature cannot use more than one reaction in response to the same trigger. You can also choose one hostile creature you can see in the aura. It must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, until the end of its next turn, its speed is halved and it cannot take reactions. During that turn, it can take either an action or a bonus action, but not both. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 229 (Homebrew)
